column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by al-Tirmidhī and others in this way.

The meaning of this hadith is that the Muslim leaves the words and deeds that are of no importance to him in matters of religion and worldly life; and by implication he devotes his effort to the ones that do concern him.
Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (1/288–289): “The meaning of this hadith is that someone whose Islam is excellent leaves the words and deeds that do not concern him

and confines himself to the words and deeds that do concern him. Yaʿnīhi (“concerns him”) means that his attention is attached to the thing and it is part of what he aims at and seeks; ʿināyah is intense concern for something. One says ʿanāhu yaʿnīhi of someone who is concerned with a thing and seeks it.

What is meant is not that he leaves what he has no concern for and no wish for as his whims and the soul's demands decide, but as the Sharīʿah and Islam decide. That is why he made it part of the excellence of Islam.

When a person's Islam is excellent, he leaves the words and deeds that do not concern him in Islam. For Islam requires doing the obligations, as mentioned in the explanation of the hadith of Jibrīl (peace be upon him), and the complete, praiseworthy Islam includes leaving the unlawful,

as he ﷺ said: ‘The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.’ When Islam is excellent, it requires leaving everything that does not concern one: the unlawful, the doubtful, the disliked, and the superfluous permissible things that one does not need;
for none of this concerns the Muslim once his Islam is complete and he has reached the level of excellence (iḥsān), which is to worship Allah the Exalted as though he sees Him,

and if he does not see Him, Allah sees him. Whoever worships Allah keeping present his nearness to Him and witnessing Him with his heart, or keeping present Allah's nearness to him and His watching over him, has made his Islam excellent,

and it follows from this that he leaves everything that does not concern him in Islam and busies himself with what concerns him in it; for from these two stations arises shyness before Allah and leaving everything one would be ashamed of.”
A person should leave what does not concern him in matters of religion and worldly life.
A person should busy himself with what concerns him of the matters of his religion and his worldly life.
Leaving what does not concern one brings rest to the soul, preserves one's time and keeps one's honour safe.
People differ in degree in their Islam.
